title: Dates & business calendar
summary: Business days around holidays, SLA due times in working hours across time zones and DST, durations and ages, recurring schedules and fiscal periods.
description:
Dates & business calendar handles the date rules that decide deadlines. Add or subtract business days around weekends and your holiday list, and compute an SLA due time from a start moment and a number of working hours: only working hours on working days count, in the time zone of the team, with daylight-saving changes handled because working hours are wall-clock times. The result comes back as a UTC instant and as local time with its offset.

It also measures durations (calendar days, business days, hours, a readable "2 years, 3 months" text and an exact age), converts a moment between time zones, lists the next occurrences of a schedule such as "the last Friday of every month at 16:00 London time", and finds the fiscal year, quarter and period of a date for a fiscal year that starts in any month, with the period, quarter and year boundaries and a label like FY2027 Q2.
uses: Set a due date 8 working hours after a ticket arrives, in the support team's time zone
Pay an invoice 10 business days after approval, skipping public holidays
Tag records with the fiscal year and quarter for reporting
setup: Install the package: the action appears in Extensibility → Workflow actions and in the workflow designer's palette under Custom actions.
Drag Dates & business calendar onto a workflow, choose the function and map its inputs; keep holidays in a data table or variable and map the list into Holidays.
Use the outputs from the data picker, e.g. {{sla_due}} for a Set SLA or Pause Until step, or {{fiscal_label}} in a title.
Try the included "Business-hours SLA (sample)" workflow from the API or its start form: it computes a due time in Pacific/Auckland working hours and the business days until then.
